title: What the CBRT bought when Turkish government bond liquidity came under pressure
bank: Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye
summary: The CBRT brought government bond purchases forward twice in 2026. The first episode followed the March geopolitical shock. The second followed September stress in domestic investment funds. Both took place within a programme originally designed to maintain the securities portfolio needed for liquidity operations. By 9 November its nominal value had reached TRY 567.9 billion, above the TRY 450 billion initially envisaged for the year. The original plan expressly allowed additional purchases. For a holder of lira bonds, the composition of purchases and the market conditions triggering them matter as much as the final portfolio size (Box 1.1, pp. 1–3).

The first TRY 78.3 billion in January and February was accumulated gradually. March and April added TRY 144.1 billion as the war increased bond-market volatility. Of the TRY 222.4 billion bought over those four months, TRY 137.4 billion comprised fixed coupons and TRY 85 billion securities indexed to TLREF or TLREFK. The portfolio rose from 2.4% of the Bank’s analytical balance sheet at the start of the year to 4.4% in April. By August, maturities and growth in the balance-sheet denominator had lowered the ratio to 3.6% during the purchase pause (Charts 1–2).

The auctions resumed on 20 August, with primary dealers participating in a route through which the Bank acquired TRY 103.8 billion of fixed-coupon domestic government securities. The Bank separately reports TRY 47 billion of additional TLREF-linked purchases after the September disruption. Gross purchases over 2026 to the reporting date reached TRY 373.2 billion, including TRY 132 billion of indexed securities. The opening stock was TRY 262.3 billion. Comparing stocks with gross purchases implies TRY 67.6 billion of net offsets over the period. The box explicitly identifies redemptions during the pause but does not itemise every offset. Chart 3 shows the stock’s weighted average maturity lengthening from 2.9 to 3.6 years. Weekly auction maturities fluctuated more than the portfolio average. Indexed instruments also carry a different interest-rate exposure from a fixed coupon of the same maturity.

The market evidence concerns two distinct prices. Chart 4 tracks volatility of the two-year benchmark yield over ten trading days. Chart 5 tracks the five-day moving average of debt-stock-weighted clean prices for TLREF-indexed bonds. Volatility rose and the indexed bonds traded below par in the spring. Both series subsequently moved towards more orderly conditions. The Bank attributes part of this to its purchases and reports that September pressure also eased. The charts contain no untreated market or adjustment for concurrent news. They support an account of how a buyer could absorb forced sales, while leaving the size and persistence of the intervention effect open. At publication, the next roadmap was due in December.

questions.question: Did purchases improve dealers’ capacity to intermediate private trades?
questions.detail: Lower observed volatility could reflect the official buyer or a broader recovery. Auction allocations, dealer turnover, bid–ask spreads and order-book depth in comparable purchased and unpurchased securities would show whether liquidity survived between auctions. That distinction matters for the cost of exiting a bond position.

questions.question: How much fixed-rate duration left the market?
questions.detail: The report gives nominal purchases, indexation and average maturity. Estimating the change in private duration exposure requires issue-level coupon schedules, reset dates, maturities and offsetting Treasury issuance. The Bank’s auction results and debt-management statistics would permit that calculation.

questions.question: Which part of the indexed-bond discount compensated investors for liquidity?
questions.detail: A clean price below par can also reflect the reset convention and the expected funding path. Reconstruct fair prices from issue terms, reference-rate fixings and contemporaneous repo funding, then compare residual discounts around auction dates.
